I'd buy the Pecron E1000LFP at $399. It meets your capacity target, uses a LiFePO₄ battery, and has a much more useful 1,800W AC output than most budget 1kWh stations. My runner-up is the Bluetti Elite 100 mini if you only need to power smaller electronics.

Pecron E1000LFP

$399.00

FactoryPure

Best overall: 1,024Wh LiFePO₄ battery and 1,800W continuous AC output. Better suited to outage backup, refrigerators, and occasional higher-power appliances. Check appliance startup requirements.

Bluetti Elite 100 mini

$379.00

BLUETTI-US · 4.8 (13 reviews)

Best for electronics: 1,004.8Wh LiFePO₄ battery, 23.6 lb, and a claimed 6,000+ cycles. Its 700W continuous output rules out most kettles, heaters, and microwaves. 
Popular Science

For either, budget roughly 800–900Wh of usable AC energy as a planning estimate: around 8 hours at 100W or 4 hours at 200W, with shorter runtimes at very low loads due to inverter overhead.

I assumed you're buying new in the U.S., with a $400 limit before tax, and prioritized general-purpose backup over weight or solar charging. I verified advertised prices, not checkout totals, and haven't independently tested either unit or confirmed warranty service quality. At $399, the Pecron will exceed $400 after sales tax in most locations.

I'd buy the Pecron E1000LFP at $399 for general-purpose backup. It has a genuine 1,024Wh LiFePO₄ battery and an 1,800W AC inverter, so it can run substantially more types of appliances than most budget stations with the same battery capacity. If you only need to keep electronics running, I'd save $20 and get the Bluetti instead.

Pecron E1000LFP

$399.00

FactoryPure

Best all-rounder: 1,024Wh, 1,800W continuous AC output. The extra inverter power is useful for a fridge's startup surge, tools, or a brief kitchen-appliance run. Check your appliance's actual requirements.

Bluetti Elite 100 mini

$379.00

BLUETTI-US · 4.8/5 (13)

Best for electronics: 1,004.8Wh LiFePO₄ battery, but only 700W continuous AC output. Good for a router, laptop, lights, or CPAP; not a kettle or space heater. Bluetti claims over 6,000 charge cycles. 
Popular Science

For either, I'd budget roughly 800–900Wh of usable AC energy as a planning estimate, not a tested result. That's about 8–9 hours at a steady 100W, or around 30–36 minutes at 1,500W on the Pecron.

I assumed you want a new, standalone station in the US, under $400 before tax, with at least 1,000Wh of actual battery capacity. These are listed Black Friday prices as of November 27, 2026; I haven't verified checkout totals, warranty service, or independently tested either unit. If $400 must include tax, the $399 Pecron won't fit.
